# Scalarization of Vector Fields
## Overview
Scalarization of Vector Fields converts multi-component vector data into single-component scalar fields to enable standard volume rendering or surface extraction techniques [S1, unofficial]. It sets itself apart from direct vector visualization methods (like [Stream Lines](4796-stream-lines.md)) by projecting the vector information onto a scalar metric, allowing the use of established transfer functions for opacity and color mapping [S1, unofficial].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family evaluate a mapping function $M(\mathbf{x})$ at sample points $\mathbf{x}$ within the volume to produce visual attributes [G]. The core mechanism involves sampling the multi-component data field at $\mathbf{x}$, decomposing or normalizing the value (e.g., extracting magnitude, direction, eigenvalues, or phase), and applying a transfer function or geometric construction to map these features to rendering parameters such as color, opacity, or primitive geometry [G].

## Subtopics

### [Helicity Visualization](8393-helicity-visualization.md)
Helicity Visualization maps the dot product of velocity and vorticity to opacity and color to identify vortices and their rotation direction in fluid flows. It sets itself apart from siblings like [Metric Scalar Field Rendering from Vector Fields](14065-metric-scalar-field-rendering-from-vector-fields.md) by explicitly leveraging the alignment between flow direction and local rotation to highlight swirling features, whereas metric methods often rely on magnitude or strain. See [Helicity Visualization](8393-helicity-visualization.md).

### [Metric Scalar Field Rendering from Vector Fields](14065-metric-scalar-field-rendering-from-vector-fields.md)
Metric Scalar Field Rendering converts vector field data into scalar values to enable standard surface or volume rendering techniques. It solves the problem of visualizing vector fields, which lack a single intensity value, by calculating metrics such as velocity magnitude, vorticity, or divergence. It differs from [Helicity Visualization](8393-helicity-visualization.md) by focusing on general magnitude-based scalarization rather than the specific alignment of curl and velocity. See [Metric Scalar Field Rendering from Vector Fields](14065-metric-scalar-field-rendering-from-vector-fields.md).

### Velocity Component Visualization
Visualizing specific components of the velocity field (e.g., x-component) to identify flow separation and reversal [S1, unofficial]. Map the smallest x velocity values (including negative values) to cyan and high opacity [S1, unofficial]. Map the largest x velocity components to yellow and near transparency [S1, unofficial].

## Background
The technique originated in early computational fluid dynamics (CFD) visualization research [G]. Volume Rendering for Computational Fluid Dynamics: Initial Results (1991) demonstrated the use of scalarization to visualize perturbation velocity fields, specifically mapping negative x-components to cyan to highlight flow separation from surfaces [S1, unofficial].
